title: Unsigned Child Process Spawned by Web Server — Lineage Tier Escalation
event_type: Process-creation telemetry (Sysmon-style Event ID 1), web-server parent spawning an unsigned child, evaluated against Part 11's lineage-tier model

fields.label: ParentChildPairFrequency
fields.value: Never observed before in this environment (0 prior occurrences over 90-day baseline)

fields.label: LineageTier
fields.value: Highly Suspicious (escalated from Suspicious solely on unsigned child signature)

callouts.explanation: Under the naive rule this field alone would fire the alert; under the revised model it only shifts the lineage tier rather than standing as a verdict on its own.
The actual output of Part 11's four-tier model — the unsigned status raised an already-rare parent-child pair from Suspicious to Highly Suspicious, which is the mechanism the fix depends on.
A web server spawning any child process at all is rare in a healthy deployment; a never-before-seen pairing is the baseline signal that a bare signature check has no way to express.
Identifies the parent as the web-server worker process itself, the exact relationship Part 16's DET-16-04 targets instead of the child binary's signature status alone.

note: This is an illustrative, conceptual field breakdown of a process-creation event and its resulting lineage-tier classification; it is not a captured screenshot and depicts no product interface.
